tasks.short: Review records and earlier reports, gather outside records, analyse test results, make the diagnosis, and record it.

steps.what: Internist reviews records and earlier reports across record screens
Internist requests outside records and letters by phone and e-mail
Internist reads the results as trend lines, where values out of range or changed sharply are flagged by fixed rules
Internist analyzes test results and examination information
Internist diagnoses the medical condition of the patient
Internist records the diagnosis and reasoning

tasks.design: The record ({OTHER}) shows a problem-oriented summary with active problems, medication and recent reports, and results with trend lines where fixed rules flag values out of range or changed sharply. Outside records come through the national exchange with the patient's consent instead of phone requests. The diagnosis is recorded on a coded problem list. Analysing and diagnosing stay with the internist; no software proposes diagnoses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were spread over screens and outside records requested by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Records show problem summaries and flagged trends; national exchanges carry outside records.
tasks.still_hard: Problem lists are often out of date.
tasks.human_edge: Connecting vague complaints into one diagnosis.

reach.learn: Whether the problem list is current.

evidence.claim: Records can show problem summaries and flag results by reference range and change.
Decision software is usually a regulated device and high-risk under the AI Act; here no software proposes diagnoses.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient visit to the diagnosis recorded; treatment is outside.
Input contract: patient consent for the exchange; fallback is phone requests.
research_questions: Are outside records available at the first visit more often?

incremental.description: Internist keeps the problem list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new patients with few records; high: complex patients with long histories.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose the medication or therapy, check interactions and doses, write the prescription, explain it to the patient, and administer or order administration.

steps.what: Internist chooses medication or therapy to treat the disease
Internist checks interactions, kidney function doses and contraindications
Internist prescribes the medication
Internist explains the medication to the patient
Internist administers or orders administration of specialized medical care

tasks.design: Medication surveillance in the prescribing module ({OTHER}) checks interactions, contraindications and doses, adjusted to the latest kidney function, while the prescription is written, so the internist does not look them up. Order sets per common diagnosis fill dose and duration. Choosing the therapy, explaining it and giving care stay with the internist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Doses for kidney function and interactions were looked up separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule-based medication surveillance runs in prescribing modules.
tasks.still_hard: Too many alerts get clicked away.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing many medicines in a frail elderly patient.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates; KNMP sets the content.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software does not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: from the diagnosis to care given; dispensing is outside.
Input contract: lab values linked to the prescribing module; fallback is looking up.

incremental.description: Internist reviews and overrides alerts that do not apply.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex patients with many alerts; high: common prescriptions with order sets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review chronic disease values before the visit, see patients in follow-up, write the visit note, write the letter to the GP, check it, and send it.

steps.what: Internist reviews chronic disease values before the visit
Internist provides and manages long-term medical care in follow-up visits
Internist writes the visit note

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.check: A validator flags any medication, dose or value in the draft that does not match the record; the internist edits and approves before saving.
loop.stop: One draft per visit; if the patient declines recording or the draft is rejected, the internist writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: The visit is told in the patient's words; a form does not capture it.

steps.what: Internist writes the letter to the general practitioner
Internist checks the final letter
Internist sends the letter to the general practitioner

tasks.design: A chronic care view in the record ({OTHER}) shows the patient's disease values (blood pressure, HbA1c, kidney function) against targets over time. With consent, a scribe drafts the visit note; a validator flags medication and values that do not match the record, and the internist approves before saving. The GP letter template pulls in the note's conclusion and medication changes; once checked, it goes to the GP through the secure exchange. Seeing patients and managing care stay with the internist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values were gathered from several screens and notes and letters typed after visits.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes the clinician validates; records show chronic care views.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can add findings that were not discussed.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing with a patient on what matters most in years of illness.
tasks.altitude: The internist validates drafts instead of typing.

reach.learn: Whether letters arrive on the day.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates before the note goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, 1,295 clinicians reported time per note falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with Tandem notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from follow-up due to the letter sent; hospital admission is outside.
Input contract: values in the record; fallback is gathering by hand.
The internist approves every note and letter.
A DPIA and works council consent come before recording.
research_questions: How long does editing drafted notes take?

approvals.approved_version: The letter as checked by the internist in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short visits; high: complex chronic patients with long notes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss results and treatments with patients, hand out patient information, draft replies to follow-up questions, and send them.

steps.what: Internist explains procedures and discusses test results with patients
Internist prepares patient information on prescribed treatments
Internist writes replies to patients' follow-up questions

loop.input: The patient's question, the record and the hospital's vetted patient information texts.
loop.output: A draft reply quoting the vetted texts.
loop.check: Every advice sentence must cite a vetted text paragraph or it is dropped; questions about new symptoms are not drafted; the internist edits and approves every reply.
loop.stop: One draft per question; if no sentence passes, the internist writes the reply.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients ask in their own words; a fixed list of answers does not match them.

steps.what: Internist sends the reply in the patient portal

tasks.design: Patient information comes from a library of vetted, guideline-based texts linked to diagnosis and treatment codes in the record, instead of writing it per patient. For follow-up questions in the patient portal, a bounded step drafts replies only from those texts; symptom questions go to the internist, and the internist approves every reply before it is sent. Discussing results stays with the internist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information sheets were assembled per patient and replies written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted patient texts exist; language models draft replies that cite them.
tasks.still_hard: Bad news must be given in person.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a patient a serious result with care.
tasks.altitude: The internist approves replies instead of writing each one.

evidence.claim: Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from results ready to the reply sent; treatment changes are outside.
Input contract: vetted texts kept by the hospital; fallback is writing replies.
Patients read portal replies as before.
research_questions: How many drafted replies does the internist change?

incremental.description: Internist suggests texts for the vetted library.

approvals.approved_version: The reply as edited and approved by the internist in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few portal questions; high: many questions after results.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The internist keeps diagnosing, prescribing, managing long-term care and discussing results; screen searching, look-ups, typed notes and letters shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An internist with more time for patients.
